claims.content: To register and process a claim submission from a Voucher Service Provider (VSP) into the VMUS system, validating mandatory information and capturing treatment details for reimbursement.

goal.raw_text: To register and process a claim submission from a Voucher Service Provider (VSP) into the VMUS system, validating mandatory information and capturing treatment details for reimbursement.

claims.content: MSIU Field Office User
The VSP has submitted the Claim (Treatment Form) to the MISU Field office, including all mandatory information such as voucher number, clinical details, diagnosis, drugs, and costs.
The claim form includes a thumb print impression from the patient, which will be compared against previous visits for the same voucher number to detect mismatches.
The MSIU Field Office User has access to the VMUS system with appropriate privileges to enter and validate claims.
The system has master data populated for VSPs, staff, syndromes, drugs, lab tests, and payment terms required to process the claim.
The voucher associated with the claim is valid and has not been previously used or flagged for fraud.
The VSP submits the Claim (Treatment Form) to the MSIU Field Office, prompting the user to initiate registration in the VMUS system.

trigger.raw_text: The VSP submits the Claim (Treatment Form) to the MSIU Field Office, prompting the user to initiate registration in the VMUS system.

claims.content: The MSIU Field Office User selects the option to submit a new Claim (Treatment Form) in the VMUS system.
The system prompts the user to enter or select the VSP Name from the VSP Master list.
The user enters the Date of Submission, which defaults to the current system date but can be adjusted if needed.
The user inputs the Number of Mentioned Forms and Number of Available Forms; the system validates that these values are numeric and that ‘No of forms’ matches ‘No of Available Forms’.
For each claim form, the user enters the Treatment Form No and Claim No (automatically generated by the system with Hospital Code suffix + 8 digits).
The system automatically populates Submitted Date and VSP Name based on prior selections.
The user scans or manually enters the Voucher No using the Bar Code reader from the voucher slip attached to the claim form.
The system captures Visit Count and Patient Type from the barcode on the voucher slip.
The user enters Patient Name, Age, Gender (selected from Male/Female), Address (with auto-population from master records where possible), and Contact No (optional).
The user selects Doctor Name from the VSP Staff Master list and enters Doctors Note if required.
If applicable, the user enters HIV Details following the format specified in the SRS attachment.
The user selects Patient Status from the Patient Status Master; if status is ‘Referral’, the system prompts for ‘Referred To’ and ‘Reason for Referral’ populated from Referral Master.
The user enters Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test results, Drugs (Name – Frequency – No of days – Qty), and Other Measures as per treatment level defined in MSIU treatment master.
The system validates all mandatory fields; if any are missing or invalid, it rejects the claim and returns it to quarantine area for correction.
The system compares the thumb impression captured on this claim form with previous visits under the same voucher number; if mismatch detected, it increments a counter and warns the user.
If more than two thumb impression mismatches occur for the same VSP, the system automatically generates a warning message and deactivates the VSP pending review.
Upon successful validation, the system calculates the Claim Amount based on the treatment matrix: First Visit Fee + Lab Test Amount + (Qty of drugs * Retail Price from Drugs Master).
The system assigns a unique Claim Number (auto-generated with hospital code suffix) and stores the claim record in the database.
The system prints a receipt document containing VSP Name, Date of Submission, No of Claims Mentioned, No of Claims Available, and detailed transaction data including Treatment Form No and Claim No.
The claim is marked as ‘Accepted’ and queued for payment processing according to agreed bi-monthly or monthly terms between MSIU and VSP.

If any mandatory information is missing or false data is detected during claim entry, the system rejects the claim and marks its status as 'Rejected' or 'Quarantine', returning it to the VSP for correction before re-submission.

If the thumb impression on the current claim form mismatches with previous visits under the same voucher number, the system increments a mismatch counter; if this occurs more than twice for the same VSP, the system automatically generates a warning and deactivates the VSP pending management review.

If the Patient Status selected is 'Referral', the system requires additional fields — 'Referred To' and 'Reason for Referral' — to be populated from the Referral Master; failure to provide these blocks claim submission.

If the Number of Mentioned Forms does not match the Number of Available Forms entered by the user, the system prevents progression until values are reconciled, ensuring data integrity before processing individual claims.
If the Voucher No scanned or entered is invalid, expired, or already used, the system halts claim registration and alerts the user that the voucher cannot be processed further.

The claim status is set to 'Accepted' and queued for payment processing according to agreed bi-monthly or monthly terms between MSIU and VSP.
A printed receipt document has been generated containing VSP Name, Date of Submission, No of Claims Mentioned, No of Claims Available, Treatment Form No, and Claim No.

If thumb impression mismatch was detected, the system has incremented the mismatch counter for that voucher; if exceeding two mismatches for the same VSP, the VSP is automatically deactivated pending review.
All mandatory fields have been validated and confirmed present; no false or missing data remains unaddressed.
Claim Amount has been calculated based on treatment matrix: First Visit Fee + Lab Test Amount + (Qty of drugs * Retail Price from Drugs Master).
Patient Status, if marked as 'Referral', includes populated 'Referred To' and 'Reason for Referral' fields sourced from Referral Master.
Number of Mentioned Forms equals Number of Available Forms, ensuring transactional consistency.
